utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we continue, there were still a few matters relating to the exhibits of yesterday that were in need for clarification. Can it be given now or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll need to do that after the first break, after I consult with Mr. Gaynor and Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll wait. But perhaps you could add one. My attention was drawn by the registrar to the fact that the CD-ROM that was provided yesterday of the video clip, that it contains B/C/S undertitling only, whereas - it's not clearly in my mind - but whereas the registrar has drawn my attention to the fact that on what we saw yesterday, we had English subtitles as well. So perhaps we could compare that it's exactly the same on that CD-ROM as what we've seen in court. We'll deal, then, with that at a later stage. Anyhow, we had, but it's quite some time ago, decided that all Sanski Most exhibits will be dealt with together, so even if no final decision would be taken today, nevertheless the clarification is needed to keep on track.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We'll check on that as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And perhaps even we should wait with that until Ms. Philpott is back, because the present registrar has not been present during all the Sanski Most evidence presented. Then I have another question for you, Mr. -- I don't know whether to -- I see with you in court today is --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, Tom Hannis, on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor. Stephen Margetts is with me, Your Honour, and he'll be leading today's witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps I'll put my next question to Mr. Margetts rather than to you. On the list of witnesses we would hear this week, we find the next witness, who is an unprotected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We find him scheduled for eight hours. On the 65 ter summary, we find him for three hours. And therefore, of course, you'll understand that I was most curious to see what was on the list that was provided today, and there is no time schedule at all. Is it three hours? Is it eight hours? Is it ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, formally it's eight hours. We will attempt to finish him earlier. So we expect six to eight hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the three hours from the 65 ter were moved?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Effectively the basis that we worked on was the eight hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your, I think at the time we filed the 65 ter we had additional viva voce witnesses from Kljuc. In the course of reshuffling, we've tried to have him introduce some of that evidence that those witnesses are now 92 bis for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That explains the change in the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if I might just inquire. It seems a very simple point. We still are not 100 per cent clear whether those time estimates are intended to include an allowance for cross-examination in accordance with the guidelines or whether they're simply talking about the Prosecution's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's always, as I understand, examination-in-chief only.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's what we understood, Your Honour. I wanted to clarify. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. It's -- in my mind, the 60 per cent are always added to get a reliable court scheduling. If there's nothing else at this moment to be raised, then I'd like Mr. Usher to bring the witness into the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear a thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Egrlic doesn't hear a thing. Could you please check whether he's on the right channel, Mr. Usher. THE USHER: He's on the right channel now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He's on the right channel. Can you now hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- may I invite you to stand up. Before giving evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of this declaration will be handed out to you by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll first be examined by Mr. Margetts, counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Margetts, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: My name is Asim Egrlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Were you born on the 27th of July, 1952 in the municipality of Kljuc in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Have you lived in Kljuc all your life, apart from a short period between 1992 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Are you by ethnicity Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to show the witness the first map that is listed on the exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. And that map would have number P ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be P221.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you put any questions -- Mr. Stewart, is there any dispute about where Kljuc is, the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Mr. Margetts. I take it that the parties agree that it's where the green spot is on the map. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could the second map be presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They would then be P222. And may I ask the parties whether the parties consider this map to depict the villages in the municipality of Kljuc? Mr. Stewart, is the Defence position that P222 depicts the villages in the municipality of Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Apparently so, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Margetts, of course, if you have any additional details to ask the witness, but this is not a matter that could keep us apart. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll refer back to that map at a later time in the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, I'm now going to run through a summary of your qualifications and work history. Please listen carefully to what I say, and when I'm finished, I'm going to ask you whether the summary that I've run through is correct. You graduated from Sarajevo university in 1977 with a Bachelor of Science and Architectural Engineering degree. In December 1977, you joined the company Sana in Kljuc, where you worked as an architectural engineer. In the period April 1979 to March 1980, you performed your compulsory military training with the JNA. You remained with the company Sana until 1986, when you set up your own private building construction engineering firm. In 1991, following the multiparty elections, you took up the position as president of the Executive Board of Kljuc Municipality. After the war, you returned to Kljuc in September 1995, where you obtained employment as president of the Municipal Chamber. After this, you were appointed mayor of Kljuc. You then gained the appointment of Minister for Energy and Industry in the cantonal government of the Una Sana canton in Bosnia. And finally, you were appointed president of the cantonal board of the SDA. In the year 2000, you opened a private enterprise specialising in architectural design, and you continue to work in your private firm to today. Mr. Egrlic, is that an accurate summary of the various positions and appointments that you have held?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd now like to deal in more detail with the period leading up to the war in Bosnia, starting with late 1990 through to early -- through 1991. During the period 1991, were you resident in Egrlici? And is Egrlici a small commune situated about two kilometres or thereabouts from Kljuc city?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Just before the multiparty elections in Bosnia in late 1990, did you join the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And what was your position in the party?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I was elected president of the municipal organisation of the Kljuc SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Was there another Muslim party in Kljuc, namely the Muslim Bosniak organisation, or the MBO?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And was Omer Filipovic the leader of the MBO?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Who was the president of the SDS party in the municipality of Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Sorry, I meant to refer to the Serb party, that is, the Serbian Democratic Party. Who was the leader of that party?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The leader of the SDS was Veljko Kondic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, prior to 1990, did you have any association with Veljko Kondic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We worked together in the same company called Sana Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And did the Serb party win more seats in the multiparty elections in Kljuc than the Muslim parties?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. The SDS had a majority in the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: After the elections, was Jovo Banjac of the SDS party appointed to the position of president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Prior to 1990, did you have any association with Jovo Banjac?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Jovo Banjac also worked in the same company, so we had daily contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: For what period of time did you have these daily contacts with Jovo Banjac?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Approximately those meetings would last between 15 and 20 minutes. We would meet in order to discuss the daily activities, since Mr. Banjac was the technical manager of the company where I also worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: For how many years did you work with Mr. Banjac at this company?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: About ten years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Was Omer Filipovic elected vice-president of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Omer Filipovic was the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly, and he was deputy to Mr. Banjac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What position did you hold in the municipal government?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: After the first multiparty election, I was elected the president of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Following the multiparty elections at the end of 1990 and prior to the start of the war in Croatia in the middle of 1991, what was the relationship like between the ethnicities in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The relationship was good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When the war started in Croatia in 1991, were there mobilisation calls to the young men of Kljuc and did the Muslims respond to those calls?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There were mobilisation calls; however, young Muslims refused to go to wage a war in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Why did they refuse to go to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They refused because they believed that an unjust war is being waged in Croatia against a people and against the dissolution of Yugoslavia, and they did not want to take sides with anybody in that war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When you say "an unjust war," why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Because from the territory of the Municipality of Kljuc and other municipalities in Bosnia and Herzegovina, first volunteers went to those front lines, and they waged this war against Croats in their own homeland.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to show the witness the next exhibit. It's the one that's actually listed fourth on the exhibit list, dated 21 September 1991, and the translation ERN is L0023457.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, do you recognise this announcement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, could that exhibit be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be P223 and P223.1 for the translation into English. I see that the translation bears the script "draft translation." I take it that it's a final translation now or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Would you like us to amend that reference?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Let's be very practical. It's now on the record that this draft translation is a final translation. You checked that. And it's the translation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, do you recognise this announcement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Were you the joint author with Mr. Filipovic of this announcement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You'll see in the middle of the page there is a heading which states "Announcement," and under that there is a paragraph which commences "The Muslim residents of Kljuc." And it proceeds to state that the Muslims of Kljuc were under no obligation to serve in the JNA units, and then refers to the issue of the constitutional order in Yugoslavia. Can you explain what the issue was that concerned you in respect of the constitutional order as at September 1991.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, above all we were concerned by the fact that the Presidency of Yugoslavia at that time was a collective body which was supposed to have command over the JNA no longer had such control. And a war broke out first of all in Slovenia and then in Croatia, and also there was a risk that this war might spread to Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the Bosniaks, the Muslims, in such circumstances found themselves in a very unenviable position, which is why we reacted in this way; which is why they didn't want to respond to the call-up from such an army, because it was no longer a Yugoslav army in the sense of the term under the Constitution of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In the announcement, you refer to the conflict in Croatia as a Serbian-Croatian conflict. If the SFRY Presidency was not functioning as a Supreme Commander, who was controlling the Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Serbia was controlling it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What effect did the failure of the Muslims to respond to the calls for mobilisation have on the relations between the ethnicities in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The Serbian Democratic Party and the Serbs, who were supporters of theirs, misunderstood this declaration, this announcement, and they interpreted it as meaning that the Bosniaks in the Municipality of Kljuc were taking sides with the Croats and did not want to participate in the conflicts with them, and this led to a deterioration of relationships and the work of the municipal -- of the Assembly organs was put into question, as well as the security situation in the territory of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Were the Muslims siding with the Croats?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The Muslims didn't respond to the mobilisation calls. What effect did this have on the ethnic mix of the soldiers that constituted the JNA units?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Given that the Muslims failed to respond to the call-up, the composition of the JNA became -- the JNA became composed of just one ethnic group, because the Serbs would respond to the call-up, so that the JNA on the whole became a Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When the volunteers returned from the Croatian front line to the Kljuc municipality, what effect did that have on the security situation in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: When the volunteers left Kljuc and returned, when they went to the battlefield in Croatia and returned, the security situation deteriorated and got worse every day, because they would leave with weapons and there were provocations and there was shooting in the town. They would leave and return with weapons. So there was shooting in the town and citizens became afraid of such behaviour, and there was a lot of fear in the territory of the municipality and a lot of disturbances.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When the volunteers returned with their weapons, did they retain possession of those weapons or did they return those weapons to the JNA stores?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They would go home with their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And in that way did the young Serbian men obtain armaments?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I've finished with that exhibit, Mr. Egrlic, so you can put the document up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to the declaration of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. When did you first hear of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I first heard about that region in mid-1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: How did you hear about the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was no secret, because Kljuc municipality had previously also been part of the Chamber of Commerce of Banja Luka, and that included 17 municipalities from the Krajina region, and initially it was claimed that the Chamber of Commerce was being formed again for commercial cooperation between municipalities in the territory of Bosnian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: That first body that was formed, was that known as the Community of Municipalities?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: At the level of the Kljuc municipality, who proposed that Kljuc should join the autonomous region?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This is a proposal that I heard Jovo Banjac, the president of the Assembly, make.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What was the view of your party, the SDA, to this proposal?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Initially the SDA thought they should accept such a proposal if it was a matter of uniting municipalities on a commercial basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When the proposal was put to transform from a Community of Municipalities to a joinder of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, what was your party's position?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We didn't accept such a proposal because we thought that this no longer amounted to forming a sort of commercial cooperation. I wasn't regionalisation in that sense. It in fact amounted to a state entity within the territory of the State of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to present the next exhibit to the witness. This is the exhibit which is the fifth exhibit on the list, with the translation -- the English ERN 01909474.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could that exhibit be given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The registrar will give it a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be P224 and P224.1 for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, I refer you to point 4, which appeared at the bottom of the first page of this document. If you could look at that paragraph where it states that "We resolutely reject the proclamation of the Autonomous Region of Krajina," and proceeds stating, "The proclamation is completely unconstitutional, unacceptable." Does that accurately set out your views in respect of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, do you recognise this statement and were you the author of this statement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I do recognise it, and yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I refer you to the second page of the document and the second full paragraph in the document, which commences just a little under halfway down that page. In this paragraph, you state that "The adoption of this proposal in respect of the autonomous region is a demonstration of force by the majority, but violence brings no solution." Can you comment on that passage?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This decision on linking up the Municipality of Kljuc with the Autonomous Region of Banja Luka was made without the knowledge of the official organs of the Municipal Assembly, and the Serbian Democratic Party, given that they had the majority in the Municipal Assembly, accepted this decision as a party and they linked up the Kljuc Municipality to the Autonomous Region of Krajina. They acted as a majority within the Municipal Assembly and they acted in a violent and an undemocratic way when they took this decision on linking up the Municipality of Kljuc to the Autonomous Region of Krajina. And we saw that this involved taking such a decision by force.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Further on in that paragraph in the final sentence, you appeal to the citizens to abstain from using this as a reason to upset the peaceful life in the area. Did you see this decision as a decision taken by one ethnicity and did you see that it was unconstitutional and could have grave effects on the peaceful life that you had previously enjoyed in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the -- Mr. Hannis did indicate at the very beginning of this morning that Mr. Margetts would be leading this witness this morning, and Mr. Margetts has kept that promise. That is a very leading question. It's in fact -- it's several leading questions wrapped into one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, would you reformulate your questions. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, in this document you state that the decision to join the autonomous region is unconstitutional, and you state that this could lead -- you request the citizens to abstain from upsetting the peaceful life in Kljuc. Can you comment on those two statements.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We thought that the decision was unconstitutional, since the usual procedure hadn't been respected. The usual procedure in the municipality wasn't followed. Secondly, it's unconstitutional because the then-Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina didn't recognise the unification of municipalities into a sort of state formation in Bosnia and Herzegovina. We believed that this decision could cause restlessness among the citizens, could cause disturbances, which is why we didn't want this decision to affect the good relationships in the territory of the Municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, if I could refer you to the last sentence on the second page of this document. It states: "We are against any mobilisation which has not been approved by the Ministry of National Defence of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Why was that? Why were you opposed to a mobilisation that was not sanctioned by the Bosnian state?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We were against such mobilisation because it wasn't in accordance with the law and the Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina, because a ministry at the level of the state had been bypassed and mobilisation was being conducted by the local authorities in the Municipality of Kljuc. And their objective was to mobilise people to be engaged in the battlefields in Croatia, which is something that we did not support. As a result, we made it quite public that we were against such mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Which party was promoting and implementing the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The SDS supported this mobilisation and believed that it was necessary to support the Serbs in certain places in the territory of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Mr. Egrlic could be shown the next exhibit, which is the document which is third on the exhibit list, dated 17 September 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That, Mr. Registrar, if I'm not mistaken, gets number P225.1 for the English and P225 for the original B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, can you take a look at this document. Do you recognise this information?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I refer you to the last sentence of the first paragraph, the first major paragraph under the heading "Information." And in respect of the declaration of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, it's stated that this policy, which is promoted by the SDS is supported by invoking the historical principle or the ethnic principle, whichever is more convenient." Can you comment on what was meant by the term "the ethnic principle"?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, should we not just make it clear with the witness what this document is before getting into the content?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course we know from the list what it's supposed to be. But Witness, could you -- Mr. Egrlic, could you tell us, if you recognise it, what is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Perhaps I should make it clear. I don't mind in the least the witness being led on such a simple point as what's in the list. It's just that, as Your Honour points out, we know, because we got the list, what it is, but nobody else listening to this case has the faintest idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know what it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is information for the public from the Muslim Bosniak Organisation, from the Municipal Committee. They were part of the Party of Democratic Action, and they were together in the coalition in the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc. This is a document which informs the public of the proclamation of the so-called Autonomous Region of Krajina by the Serbian Democratic Party, or rather, it informs them of the fact that the Municipality of Kljuc is joining the autonomous region. And it also states our view of this event, and we inform the public in this document about the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, the author of this document is Omer Filipovic, the vice-president of the municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Returning to the final sentence at the bottom of the first major paragraph. Why did Mr. Filipovic refer to the ethnic principle being invoked in the context of this declaration of the autonomous region?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, he said that because as far as the Municipality is Kljuc is concerned and its link to the Autonomous Region of Krajina, this was done without the agreement of the Bosniaks and their political representatives from the municipality, and in fact the Bosniaks in that area were ignored and their opinion on the matter was also ignored. So in fact this ethnic principle was applied. This means that if one ethnic group supported the idea that the Municipality of Kljuc should join the autonomous region, this meant that the matter had then been settled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, it may be a detail. You said this document was a document by Omer Filipovic. I see "Muhamed Filipovic." Is that something to be ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That was my error.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, can you refer to the signature on the bottom of this page. Do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is Mr. Muhamed Filipovic's signature. He was the vice-president of the municipal organisation of the Muslim Bosniak Organisation in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Was his brother the president of that association, that is, was his brother Omer Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I make a -- just a simple practical suggestion. Again, we can see from the list which we have in advance the method by which apparently this particular content was disseminated to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- I just had the same in my mind. It gives information. Could you please clarify that, whether -- because now we have a piece of paper where the list says something in addition to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, was this document distributed in the Municipality of Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This document was information for the general public which was read out on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd like to refer you to the sentence that starts at the bottom of the first page and proceeds over into the second page, and it states: "Politics and democracy entail dialogue and tolerance. Politics and democracy as interpreted by the SDS entails dictates, ultimatums and intolerance." Does that accord with your views as to how politics should have been conducted in Kljuc and the failings of the SDS in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: When it came to this association of Kljuc with the autonomous region, we believed that the opinion of Bosniaks should be heard and respected, given the fact that in the territory of Kljuc municipality there was a great number of Bosniak residents and given the fact that their rights were not respected when this decision was made unilaterally by just one political party. That's why we believed that their -- that tolerance and democracy had been bypassed and that this decision had been made unilaterally respecting the will of only one ethnic group. We believed that the other ethnic groups should have been consulted and that their will should have also been respected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: As at September 1991, what did you believe the annexation of the Municipality of Kljuc to this Serbian Autonomous Region would lead to?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was clear by that time that the establishment of the autonomous region - with all of the bodies that had been established already, with the army that had already existed at the time - that it was a paralegal state in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that it was against the interests of the Bosniak people and that ultimately this could lead to the deterioration of political and security situation in the Municipality of Kljuc and even in Bosnia and Herzegovina as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to show the witness the next exhibit. Now, this one will be found as the exhibit four from the bottom on the first page of the exhibit list, and the date that's ascribed to it is 1 December 1991. The document itself is undated. And the translation reference is L005-7782.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, this would have number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be P226 and P226.1 for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, can you have a look at that document. I refer to the second paragraph on the first page -- sorry. In light of Mr. Stewart's request that we identify the nature of the documents, I'll proceed to do that. This document purports to be a decision --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, before we continue. On the first line of the original, I clearly see a date, the 10th of April, 1991. In the English translation, I do not see any date at all. Is this explained by that it is a draft translation or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is clearly an error. We will have that rectified. This is intended to be a final translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's I think the third time in two days now that by reading for ten seconds a document and comparing it with the original that differences are easily identified. I would prefer if the parties would do that themselves and correct it prior to presenting the evidence and these translations in court. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we will attend to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: This is a decision signed by Jovo Banjac and appears to be the proposal from the SDS party to put to the Municipal Assembly the issue of the joinder to the autonomous region. Mr. Egrlic, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When did you first see this proposal?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I saw it in front of the municipality building. The Assembly meeting was held with this being an item on the agenda, so this was discussed by the Assembly in order to arrive at a final decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Earlier you stated that the usual procedure was not followed by the SDS in putting this decision to the Assembly, then voting for it. What was the usual procedure that was followed and how was that procedure avoided by the SDS in regard to this issue?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The bypassing of the procedure referred to the fact that a decision was made to join the Municipality of Kljuc to the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina without a proper Assembly meeting. Once we learnt about that and once the information was disseminated to the general public, they decided to present this decision to the Municipal Assembly for its confirmation, and this is the proposal of the decision which was put on the agenda of the Assembly meeting. The Assembly heard this decision and made a decision on whether to adopt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When you said it wasn't a proper Assembly meeting, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The procedure was not followed because a unilateral decision by one party meant that the Municipality of Kljuc was annexed to the autonomous region in mid-1991 without this issue having been discussed at a meeting of the Municipal Assembly. It was only after we reacted and after we informed the general public about that that this issue was properly discussed as an item on the agenda of the Municipal Assembly meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You stated that you worked with Jovo Banjac, the president of the municipality, for some years. When this autonomous region was proclaimed, did you discuss this with him? And if so, what did he say about it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We discussed this on several occasions. During the preparations for the Municipal Assembly meeting, his position was that the Municipality of Kljuc had to join the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina. They claimed at the time that this was actually an organisation of municipalities that would promote economic growth and intermunicipal cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When you say that he said he had to implement this decision, did you think he had any choice in the matter?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think he had a choice, because other municipalities bordering on the Kljuc municipality territory had already arrived at such a decision. And I'm talking about the municipalities with a large majority of SDS members in their respective municipal assemblies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Are you saying that Mr. Banjac, as president of the municipality, was bound to follow the policies of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's a pretty leading question, Your Honour. It's apparent -- I won't go into it, because it's quite obvious from what this entire case is about, it's apparent that there's quite a big jump from the witness's answer to Mr. Margetts's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there is a jump. Could you proceed by smaller steps and less leading, because this is part of the core of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, did you discuss this matter with Veljko Kondic, who you also had worked with for a number of years?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. During the preparations for this meeting at the interparty council, we all put forth or positions and opinions on this matter. Mr. Kondic was adamant in his belief that they could reach that decision with the votes of only one party member, because they had a large majority. And he also believed that this had been implemented already at the beginning of the year and this would be just a confirmation of the decision that had already been adopted by the SDS MPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, in your answer, you state that the decision had already been implemented at the beginning of the year. Can you clarify that. Are you referring to the decision to join the Community of Municipalities, or are you referring to the decision to join the Autonomous Region of Krajina that was presented outside the usual procedures of the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Actually, there's no major difference between the two decisions. Initially, in the initial stages, the name was different; however, the essence of the matter is the same. And the Kljuc municipality joined first by the decision of the Municipal Board of the SDS and later on when we reacted and said that the procedure was not followed in accordance with the statute of the municipality, this decision was put forward at the Assembly meeting and it was confirmed by the members of the Municipal Assembly, who were members of the SDS party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Whilst it may have turned out that the decision to join the Community of Municipalities and the decision to join the autonomous region were effectively the same, was it not your perception that the joinder of the Community of Municipalities was acceptable because that was limited to economic associations?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, what Mr. Margetts is doing now is he's putting a very leading question for the simple reason that he doesn't like the answer that he got to the previous question, so he's now trying to get the answer that he wanted, which is not the answer that the witness gave, by putting a leading question and effectively to reverse or nullify the answer that he doesn't like. And that's not a proper way to proceed in examination of a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In the earlier part of the testimony, the witness, of course, said something about the difference between the two, so to that extent there could be some confusion which Mr. Margetts is entitled to clarify. Perhaps the way in which it is done could be more -- and I'll just reread the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, with respect, I'd suggest that we need to be very clear that there is in fact confusion, there is in fact a difference, because at the moment we don't see it. The witness has made it quite clear that there were different names. I think the Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond phrase used -- the name was -- "Initially, in the initial stages, the name was different; however, the essence of the matter is the same." That's what the witness has very clearly said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that's not what exactly was said in his earlier testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, with respect then, I do suggest that we need to be absolutely clear that there is genuine confusion to be cleared up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll deal with that in the last two minutes before the break. If you'd please now go to your next subject and I'll find the source.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we oppose Mr. Stewart's application on the basis that we have merely been repeating what was said in the earlier testimony and what is set out clearly in the documentation that the witness has confirmed represents his opinion. If Your Honour would allow me, could I proceed just to clarify this matter in the next few questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you would give the source of where you said that, the earlier testimony. If you could give page and line to Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, might -- --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll do the following: We're next to a break anyhow. I'll ask the witness to leave the courtroom so that we can discuss this procedural issue. We'll settle the matter, and then after the break, Mr. Egrlic, your examination will continue. And the break will be -- it depends a bit on how much time we'd need for the procedural issue, but something close to half an hour. Mr. Egrlic, you may follow the usher out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, could you please at the point earlier in the testimony where the witness made a distinction between accepting -- well, let's say a kind of economic cooperation in the area and that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to apologise to the Court. The difficulty is this, that the transcript I have before me does not have the capacity to scroll back. I can refer to the previous exhibits that have been shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you'd find the exhibits, I'll try to find the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're very distressed to find that equality of arms, or inequality of arms, might mean that we have this exhibit on the Defence side but the Prosecution don't. It could be -- I'm not sure whether the computer to Mr. Hannis's right has that facility. We have a laptop on the table that does have that facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that under normal circumstances the Prosecution would have an opportunity to do the same. If there's any fundamental problem, then -- and if it could not be solved, then, of course, the Chamber will look after the equality of arms, but ... Mr. Margetts, if you'd refer to the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The document is P224.1, and the paragraph that was specifically referred to was paragraph 4 of that document, where Mr. Egrlic had stated that he and the SDA party "resolutely reject the proclamation of the Autonomous District of Krajina as a successor of the Community of Municipalities and judge this act to be completely unconstitutional and unacceptable."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the transcript where -- I think it's -- it starts at page 13, approximately in the middle, where it's explained that it started as a Chamber of Commerce --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, someone is calling. Well, it seems not to be a mobile phone, because they would be seized anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I make this practical suggestion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It is possible for me to elicit an explanation from the witness in a form, I'm sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do we get now? I get on my earphones conversations of other people. Oh, no, I see. Yes. Okay, that's settled now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- in a form that I'm sure will be acceptable to Mr. Stewart, it's not necessary for me to lead him on this issue. I didn't expect Mr. Stewart's objection, given the previous evidence. But since he has objected, I'm quite happy to deal with this issue without leading him on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stewart, page 14, line 6: "We didn't accept such a proposal because we thought that this no longer amounted to forming a sort of commercial cooperation. It wasn't regionalisation in that sense. It in fact amounted to a state entity within the territory of the State of Bosnia and Herzegovina." That would clearly, I would say, explained where what was presented as commercial cooperation turned out, at least in the view of the witness, turned out to be a state within the state. And therefore, if he later says that it was all the same -- well, of course, I'm now summarising and perhaps not doing justice to the details of what he said -- there's certainly a matter which is a matter that would need further clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- I thought a moment ago Mr. Margetts said that he wasn't pursuing the matter. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm just saying that you made an objection. If Mr. Margetts does not want to pursue the matter, fine. If you can settle it during the break, fine. But we'll not stop him from seeking further clarification if he wishes to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, could I also say, Your Honour that, we wouldn't mind a few quiet minutes to sort this out, because we wondered over the last few minutes whether we're operating in a courtroom or a telephone exchange, and simply sorting out what's on the transcript where and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I gave you some clues.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, thank you, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll hear from the parties upon return. We'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we resume with the examination of the witness, is there any need to further expound on what we discussed before the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We've had discussions with Defence counsel during the break, and we're content with the way we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed, and the Chamber is happy that you resolved the matter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, in early 1991, when the Community of Municipalities was formed, did the SDA object to Kljuc being a part of the Community of Municipalities?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: At the beginning it did not object, since the explanation was that it was an association of municipalities for commercial reasons, and Kljuc had previously also been part of the Banja Luka region, and the headquarters of the Chamber of Commerce were located in Banja Luka, so it would be logical for those municipalities to remain within that Chamber of Commerce.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: So insofar as the organisation was formed for commercial reasons, you had no objection to it.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When the proposal was put to join the Autonomous Region of Krajina, you did object. What was it you objected to about the joinder to the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We objected to joining the autonomous region because this no longer seemed to be a matter of associating municipalities for the purpose of commercial cooperation. It resembled a sort of state within Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was beginning to resemble a sort of state within Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Bosniaks did not support this, which is why we stated and we made it known that we were not in favour of such an organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to show the witness the next exhibit, and this is the exhibit that appears sixth on the exhibit list, with the translation ERN L0023471.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would get the number --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number will be P227 and P227.1 for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This is an official statement from the Muslim Bosniak Organisation in which it is stated that they support the Party of Democratic Action. It has to do with the political and security situation in the territory of the Municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, was this document distributed to the citizens of Kljuc or was its content communicated to the citizens of Kljuc in or around September 1991?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They were informed about it over Radio Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd like to refer you to the first sentence in the second paragraph, which states that "The Muslim Bosniak association is opposed to any arming of people which may fall outside the context of orders issued for mobilisation of the Territorial Defence or reserve police." In September 1991, what was your knowledge of the arming of the people in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This was a reaction to individuals being armed, and that was taking place at that time in the territory of the Municipality of Kljuc. And this is why the Party of Democratic Action reacted in this way and later the Muslim Bosniak Organisation reacted in this way too, because it was noticed that the Serbian population was being armed in two ways: Firstly, a mobilisation was being carried out and weapons were being distributed which were then taken to people's homes; and secondly, in certain areas it was noticed that weapons were being delivered by military helicopters. This is why we stated that this was not the appropriate way to preserve the peace in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I refer you to the third paragraph in this document, which states as follows: "We use this opportunity to invite representatives of other peoples and political organisations to join open interparty talks as we strongly believe that this is the only way to reach desired effects. Violence would bring nothing but chaos, and in the end people would still have to talk to each other." I also refer you to the first sentence of the last substantial paragraph on page 2, which reads: "We want to talk around a table, not over the barrel of a gun." Can you comment on those statements.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: In this way, we were attempting to organise a discussion about this matter, given that the security and political situation had deteriorated. We wanted to speak about this openly, and we wanted to attempt to deal with the situation and resolve the difficulties and avoid having the population armed, as we thought that this was to -- this was not useful in the area. We thought that it would be normal to try and preserve the peace in the area and to preserve the good relationships. We attempted to do this through interparty discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What was the response of the representatives of the SDS to your attempts to discuss the security issues in the context of interparty discussions?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: All political representatives responded to this proposal for discussions apart from the SDS representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Egrlic. I've finished with that document. In 1991 and 1992, what positions did Radoslav Brdjanin hold?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, could the question put to me be more specific?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please reformulate your question, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, do you know of a man named Radoslav Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In 1991, was he a deputy in the Serbian Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And when the Autonomous Region of Krajina was formed, what position did Radoslav Brdjanin hold?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: He was the President of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When did you first hear of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was around mid-1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Did Brdjanin communicate with the SDS representatives in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: How did he communicate with them?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, he communicated with them, since people from the SDS went to joint meetings in Banja Luka, and he communicated with them on the phone by using the fax, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When you say he communicated by using the fax, did you ever see any facsimile that he sent to the representatives in the SDS in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I saw one such fax.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When you saw that fax, how did you come to see a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was probably received by -- because of a mistake made by the secretary. She brought the fax to my office with the other mail, probably by mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When you received it, what did you do with it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As I saw that the fax wasn't for me, I made a copy and I returned the original to Mr. Banjac through the secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to show the witness the next exhibit, which is the next one following -- under P227. It's dated 29 October 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That will then be P228 for the original in B/C/S and P228.1 for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Is this the facsimile that you received?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You say you copied this document. Did you retain the copy you made of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems an obvious correction. Mr. Margetts refers to it as a fax. In fact, it's really -- we suggest it's fairly obviously a telex, because it says so, apart from anything else, and that is consistent with the format. We might as well have that cleared up, in case we're wrong about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We might have almost forgotten about the existence of telexes, but it very much has the appearance of a telex.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, we have referred to this document as a facsimile. Is this document in fact a telex?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is the document as you copied it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the document that I copied and that I had with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was there a stamp on it already when you copied it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's not a telex. It's then a telefax copy of a telex, I take it, because otherwise the stamp could not be there, because stamps cannot be put on a telex. It seems that -- at least, it has the appearance - but perhaps the parties could discuss it over the next break - it seems to be a telex which then has further been transmitted, perhaps through telefax. Although there's no ID of any telefax -- no dates, no times. Unless the stamp -- well, the witness said the stamp was on it already when he copied it. Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the next few questions, I'd just like to clarify exactly what the status of this particular version of that document is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I was too eager, perhaps. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, the copy of this document that you had in 1991, what happened to it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, after a certain period of time, they started implementing the items that have been listed in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, at this stage I'm just referring to the physical piece of paper that you held in your hand. Did you take that home with you? And if so, what happened to the document and where is it today?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I took it home with me, but my house was set on fire and it burnt down, as did other objects and items there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: However, the document you have before you today is another copy of that document that you saw in 1991.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Did you speak to Mr. Banjac about this document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I had seen the document and that the contents of the document seemed to amount to introducing a state of emergency, which is only appropriate in a time of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What did he say to you in response to your comments?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: He said that this was an order from above, and he joked. When I asked whether Mr. Brdjanin was really of this opinion, he said, "Forget about Brdjo. Brdjo is mad." And that was the end of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Whilst his response was nonchalant, did subsequent events appear to indicate that this document was a document to be considered seriously?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of this document, a number of steps were taken by the SDS, the Serbian Democratic Party, so that in the forthcoming period these items were implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Were most of the items listed, numbered 1 to 14, implemented by the Kljuc SDS?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You'll note, Mr. Egrlic, in the first paragraph of the document there's a reference to a meeting of all municipal presidents on 26 October 1991 in Banja Luka which was chaired by Dr. Karadzic. Did you discuss with Mr. Banjac whether or not he attended this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't, but I knew that he was in contact with him, since he would travel to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to show the witness the next exhibit and that is the next one on the exhibit list, dated 31 October 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, I don't have the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be P229 and P229.1 for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, I'll repeat the question: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Are you the joint author of this document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Was the content of this document communicated to the people of Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It -- the contents of the document were made known over the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Can I refer you to the second paragraph, and in particular the last sentence in the second paragraph. The document refers to the telex which we have just seen and marked as Exhibit P228 and summarises the contents of this telex as being a "direction to organise life in conditions of war." Is that an accurate statement of what you considered the telex from Brdjanin dated 29 October 1991 to be?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In response to that telex, you drafted this document and made this plea to the people of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Can I refer you to the second page of the document and the last two paragraphs that appear there, and I'll quote those paragraphs and I'll ask for your comment in relation to them. You stated: "We cry out in plain language: Let those who want to wage war, let the war move into their homes but without us, the Muslims of Kljuc. We are happy with the way things are. They have learned to live honestly and modestly and even in this crisis are managing without the war or the results of war. "Therefore, let this address of ours be yet another appeal for peace, even though we know that it will not echo far or see the light of day because there are forces whom the information blockade suits fine. That is why this is the last plea with which we ask those whose minds have been clouded by Mars to come to their senses." Mr. Egrlic, what did you intend to communicate by this plea, and to whom was this plea directed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was directed to those forces from the Serbian Democratic Party which entered ever deeper into the preparations for war in the territory of Kljuc municipality and to all the citizens. The aim was to provide them with information as to what was going on in the territory of Kljuc and what activities were being undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And by communicating with the citizens, what were you hoping that the citizens' reaction to this communication would be?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We were hoping that the healthy forces that still existed in all the ethnic groups would condemn these activities and that the system of armament would be interrupted and that people would not be dragged into a war situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I refer you back to the last sentence of the second paragraph, where you stated that the facsimile from Brdjanin was tantamount to "organising life in conditions of war." When you wrote that, were you referring to the items 1 to 14 [Realtime transcript read in error: "4"] and in particularly, were you referring to the direction to set up a command of the town and to set up round-the-clock duty?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. All of that mostly referred to the activities that were being undertaken as if there was a war. The introduction of the town command meant the interruption of work of all the legally and democratically elected bodies of government. In practical terms, this was the introduction of a military administration in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Who controlled that military administration?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was the Crisis Staff of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You saw this order from Brdjanin. Did you consider that this military administration was controlled by the Regional Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You saw in this telex that the order followed a meeting in Banja Luka on the 26th of October with Dr. Karadzic. Who did you think ultimately controlled this military administration?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, before this question is pursued, we need to be very clear that this witness is a witness of fact. He is not here as an expert witness; he is not here to express opinions, unless those opinions are based on facts within his knowledge. So the basis of any such question where his opinion is being sought must concentrate on whether in the first place he knows of any facts. And then he should tell the Tribunal what facts he knows and not stray into opinion, which we've had in the past sometimes in the case, matters of speculation or views which are simply not based on fact. And it is important in these critical areas that that's the way the matter is approached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Margetts, would you lay a proper factual foundation for any questions about who controlled who. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, when you received the facsimile of 29 October 1991, did you read it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Did you observe that the order from Brdjanin was made following a meeting with Karadzic on 26 October 1991?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: On the basis of that fact, did you come to a conclusion as to whether or not Karadzic knew of these 14 steps that were set out in this document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It says on the document that it was drafted in agreement with Mr. Karadzic, so it is beyond any dispute that he knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When you read that document, did you see --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could that document be returned to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: That is Exhibit P228.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When you read that document, Mr. Egrlic, did you see that it is headed "Order of the SDS Sarajevo"?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When you read "Order of the SDS Sarajevo," who did you think constituted the leadership in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I can see from the document that the leadership of the party drafted this order and forwarded it to the lower levels, down to the municipal committees or boards. And the leader of the SDS at the time was Mr. Karadzic. And in his inner circle was Mrs. Plavsic, Mr. Krajisnik, Mr. Koljevic, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When you read the words "Order of the SDS Sarajevo," who did you think in the leadership in Sarajevo was ordering that this take place?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I thought that it was the president [Realtime transcript read in error: "Presidency"] of the SDS who had obviously discussed it with his associates and agreed on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Just to clarify that previous answer. It says: "I thought it was the Presidency of the SDS." Did you say "Presidency" or did you say "president"?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The Presidency, headed by Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Question number one is what he said. Question number two is what he chooses to give as his answer now. I don't know, of course, but sitting to my left is somebody that does know. We believe he did say "president." So first of all, we need to establish what he did say in the first answer; and then if he wants to change it or expand it and so on, then at least the Trial Chamber can see that that's what he's doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first ask you: When you first answered that question for the first time, did you say "president" or did you upon the additional question by Mr. Margetts expound your answer and say "Presidency," headed by Mr. Karadzic? What was your first answer? I'm not saying whether it's right or wrong. That's not the issue. I'd just like to know. Otherwise, we have to replay the tapes. What was your first answer, that it was obviously the president or the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I first said that it was the president with his associates, and his associates were members of the Presidency of the party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, there's always an opportunity for the parties to -- let me just scroll back for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters may confirm that it was "the president" the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for the confirmation by the interpreters. I'll just reread the part. So the main distinction between the first answer is that it was the president with his associates, and the second answer was the Presidency, headed by the president. That has been clarified. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, since we have had a break to clarify the record, I'd just like to refer back to line 11.34.07, and there's a reference there to the numbers 1 to 4. I think that's an interpretation error. The transcript should read "1 to 14."

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, we agree with that, Your Honour. We remember that was what was said and that's what it appeared on the transcript. So we agree with that correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's then corrected. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, you referred to the president and his associates. Who were his associates?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikola Koljevic, Mrs. Plavsic, Mr. Karadzic. Those were the people who were the top of the leadership of the SDS party in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, I asked you about the president and his associates, and we may have a misunderstanding here. When I was referring to the president, I was referring to the president of the party, Dr. Karadzic, not the president of the Assembly, Momcilo Krajisnik. Who were the associates of the president of the party, Mr. Karadzic, that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Members of the Presidency of the party, the individuals whose names I have mentioned. In addition to their duties in the state bodies, they were also members of the SDS leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, I'm sorry to ask you this again, and I know you've named various people as the associates of Mr. Karadzic, but I need to just clarify this matter, because I think there may have been some misunderstanding earlier. So I'll just ask you to state again who were these associates of Mr. Karadzic that you were referring to. If you could just name them again.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I meant Mrs. Plavsic, Mr. Nikola Koljevic, and Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was about -- I don't know whether you have the same in your mind or not. I'll let you first see and then we'll see whether it's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We'll see if same minds think alike, Your Honour. Mr. Margetts has find finally got the answer that he had to keep on casting his line into the water for. It is improper of Mr. Margetts, we suggest, to have introduced the name "Mr. Krajisnik" into the question that began: "Mr. Egrlic, I asked you about the president and his associates. We may have a misunderstanding here. When I was referring to the president, I was referring to the president of the party, Dr. Karadzic, not the president of the Assembly, Momcilo Krajisnik." We perceive that as a deliberate introduction of Mr. Krajisnik's name into the question, and that was -- the harm had been done by the time the question was asked, and I didn't object because it's been done and it's apparent what has been happening, and then when we cross-examine and/or when we make our submissions later in the case, this whole passage will have to be looked at it. But we will ask Mr. Margetts -- it was perhaps not consciously deliberate to do it that way, but to be extremely cautious. Mr. Margetts knew what he was looking for here as the answer, and it required the utmost care to make sure that the question was not formulated in such a way as to signal the answer, because these are the critical areas of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although it was in the first time, as far as I remember, that Mr. -- the name of Mr. Krajisnik was mentioned by the witness a couple of times before that. So it's not a new introduction, although it was in this question newly introduced. But I have a totally different question for the witness, although perhaps related, because that's the basis of the whole part of this examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I respond to Mr. Stewart's comments?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If there's anything to be added --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I appreciate that in some circumstances Mr. Stewart would be correct, but in the specific circumstances of this question and this answer, Mr. Stewart's comments, I don't think, have any weight at all, the reason being that there was clearly an error in the answer.
